message:
I remember the day I decided to talk to my grandkids about being prepared for anything. They were more interested in their video games than my go-bag demonstration. I tried to make it fun, showing them snacks and water bottles, but all they could do was roll their eyes.  

Then, one of them asked, "But Grandma, what if we just stay indoors and play?" It hit me that their idea of safety looked so different from mine. In the end, we compromised. We made a plan that included a family board game night in our safe space. I realized that preparedness doesn’t just mean having things ready; it’s about making it meaningful for them too.  

Have you ever had a moment like that with your family?
